## Observed Facts

Data Scope: BGL, 2005-06-03 to 2006-01-04, 4,747,963 Log Entries in total [E1]. No other filters unless stated.

- **KERNEL is the biggest by volume.** It has 4,324,651 of the Log Entries [E2]. 626,450 of those are at level FATAL [E4]. KERNEL makes up 626,450 of the 855,195 FATAL Log Entries [E4].
- **APP is second for FATAL.** It has 228,536 FATAL Log Entries [E4]. That is all of its 228,536 Log Entries [E2].
- **MMCS leads on ERROR.** It has 88,529 of the 112,355 ERROR Log Entries [E5]. It has only 3 FATAL Log Entries [E4].
- **DISCOVERY has the most SEVERE.** It has 18,324 of the 19,213 SEVERE Log Entries [E6]. It also has 23,825 ERROR Log Entries [E5].
- **Smaller components with a high share of severe levels:**
  - MONITOR has 1,665 FAILURE Log Entries [E7] out of 1,681 [E2].
  - LINKCARD has 206 FATAL Log Entries [E4] out of 1,170 [E2].
  - HARDWARE has 873 SEVERE Log Entries [E6] out of 5,148 [E2].

## Hypotheses

- **Priority 1: KERNEL.** It has by far the most FATAL Log Entries, so it ranks first on measured frequency.
- **Priority 2: APP.** Every one of its entries is FATAL, which suggests one repeating failure pattern. I haven't checked the messages.
- **Priority 3: MMCS and DISCOVERY.** These two dominate ERROR and SEVERE. Their counts are lower, but they are still large.
- **Watch list: MONITOR, LINKCARD and HARDWARE.** Volumes are low, but severe levels make up most of the entries for MONITOR and a large share for the other two.
- Many FATAL Log Entries may come from a few repeated events or a few nodes. I haven't measured this, so the true number of distinct problems may be far smaller than the counts suggest.

## Unknowns

- **Distinct problems:** Log Entries are not incidents. I haven't grouped by message, node or time, so I can't say how many separate problems there are.
- **Trend:** I haven't checked whether KERNEL or APP FATAL volume is growing, recurring or a one-off burst.
- **Impact:** The logs can't establish financial loss, downtime or customer impact.
- **Level semantics:** I haven't verified that the FATAL level means the same thing for every component.

## Next Step

Run a `trend` on KERNEL and APP FATAL Log Entries. Then run a `count_by` on node and alert_tag for them. This will show whether the volume is a single burst or a concentrated source. If it is, the action is narrower than "fix KERNEL".
